content: 1. Conduct annual screenings for depressive symptoms in all individuals diagnosed with diabetes. For those with a prior history of depression, perform these assessments more frequently. Utilize age-appropriate and validated screening tools to ensure accuracy, and recognize that individuals who screen positive may require further comprehensive evaluation. 2. Consider assessing for depression when diabetes-related complications are diagnosed or when there are significant changes in the individual's medical status, as these situations may increase the risk of depressive symptoms. 3. Refer individuals exhibiting depressive symptoms to behavioral health professionals or healthcare providers trained in evidence-based treatments for depression. This referral should be integrated into a collaborative care approach involving the diabetes treatment team to ensure comprehensive management of both conditions.
